page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the running head at the top and the catchword at the foot right. Left margin shows only bleed from the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: perempto ab Orœte Persa, cum fuisset omnium Græcorũ tyrannorum in eam ufq; ætatem splendidissimus, in res ejus successit Mæandrius quidam, ejusdem procurator, de quo multa Herodotus. Cui operâ Otanis Persæ ex voluntate Darii regis disjecto & profugo surrogatus Sylofon Polycratis frater, & simul Samus contra mentem Darii graviter afflicta. Hic asper ingenio durius civitatem pressit. Quem mortuum in dominatu excepit Æaces filius clientela Persica fretus, sed non multò post dominatu dejectus ab Aristagora Milesio totam Ioniam contra Persas commovente. Ita Samus libertati restituta, & reliquis Ionibus sociata. Verum à morte Aristagoræ, Dionysio Phocensi partes ejus sustinente, cum jam classis Ionum in procinctu esset, ac sese ad pugnam pararet contra Phœnices à Dario armatos, Samiarum navium præfecti persuasi ab Æace nuper tyrannide exuto, in ipso prælio jam conserto socios deseruere: quorum exemplo alii quoque turbati fugæ se dederunt. Soli Chii in pugnâ constantes perstitere, navibus freti centum, iisque milite & instrumento necessario bene instructis, donec fessi labore, plerique etiam navibus in prælio amissis, ipsi quoque fortunæ cesserê. Tum Mi-

page.notes: Printed text ends with "Tum Mi-" and the catchword "letus" stands below the last line at the right. The left-edge marks (such as "nferis", "ɪɛ", "cɔɔ") are bleed from the adjacent page and were not transcribed. A small "3" appears at the bottom left near the text; it is doubtful whether it is a gathering signature, so I left it out. Ligatures ss and ff have been read as ss in "pressit", "fessi" and "persuasi". "Orœte" is read from a small, faint scan and is uncertain.
